commands.review_summary:
The branch moves usage-cost cache `pricingFingerprint` to the cache file level, strips it from serialized entries, sets the active fingerprint before refresh writes, and adds a cold round-trip test.

PR surface: Source +38, Tests +62. Total +100 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. source-level: current main writes `pricingFingerprint` on every cache entry, and the PR diff shows a mixed-cache path where old entries can inherit the new file-level fingerprint after reload. I did not run tests because this review was constrained to read-only inspection.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] A narrow automated repair can preserve the PR's useful deduplication while fixing the mixed-fingerprint cache invalidation bug.

target.title: fix(infra): deduplicate pricing fingerprint in usage-cost cache
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The per-agent usage-cost cache stores the full `pricingFingerprint` string (~2.7 KB) on every entry. The fingerprint is identical across all entries, so on large caches it dominates the file — ~57% of a 142 MB cache as pure duplication.

Closes #99511

## Root Cause / Fix

Every `UsageCostCacheFileEntry` carried a copy of the same `pricingFingerprint` string. The fix stores it once at the `UsageCostCacheFile` level and strips it from entries before serialization. On load, `normalizeUsageCostCache` transparently restores the fingerprint to entries from the file level, so all internal code reading `entry.pricingFingerprint` is unchanged. The active fingerprint is persisted before every cache write in `refreshCostUsageCacheForPath`.

**+6 lines changed. No internal references touched.**

## Evidence

### Real production function proof (cold cache round-trip)

Created two session transcript files, ran `refreshCostUsageCache()`, then inspected the serialized cache file:

```text
=== Real cache file proof (#99511) ===
File level pricingFingerprint: PRESENT ✅
  length: 113 bytes
Entries with pricingFingerprint: 0/2 ✅
Entries total: 2
File size: 1,593 bytes
```

The fingerprint is stored once at the file level; entries are stripped.

### Pricing-change round-trip

Existing test `invalidates durable aggregate cache when gateway pricing cache changes` verifies that changing the pricing config correctly invalidates the cache. Setting the active fingerprint before each write ensures the cache is rebuilt when the pricing model changes.

### Before/after serialization comparison

```text
Before: { version: 4, files: { "a.jsonl": { ..., pricingFingerprint: "sha256:abc...", ... }, "b.jsonl": { ..., pricingFingerprint: "sha256:abc...", ... } } }
            ↑ duplicated on every entry

After:  { version: 4, pricingFingerprint: "sha256:abc...", files: { "a.jsonl": { ... }, "b.jsonl": { ... } } }
            ↑ stored once at file level
```

## Change Type
- [x] Performance fix
## Scope
- [x] Infrastructure (usage-cost cache)
## Security Impact
- New permissions? No · Secrets changed? No · New network calls? No
